staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced the crash from this preserved vulnerable checkout. Its `xinclude.c` line map matches the saved AddressSanitizer path at `xmlXIncludeLoadFallback` line 2002, `xmlXIncludeIncludeNode` lines 2216 and 2267, `xmlXIncludeDoProcess` line 2471, and `xmlXIncludeProcessTreeFlagsData` line 2524.

classification.classification_note: The saved witness reaches libxml2's XInclude fallback path with `XML_PARSE_XINCLUDE | XML_PARSE_NOXINCNODE` enabled. In one reused-`newctxt` recursive pass, a fallback-child include entry is marked with `emptyFb = 1`, then `xmlXIncludeIncludeNode` frees its `ref` node under the `XML_PARSE_NOXINCNODE` branch without clearing `emptyFb` or `ref`. A later reused-context pass therefore re-enters the same third-phase predicate on `emptyFb != 0`, reloads the dangling pointer from `newctxt->incTab[nr]->ref`, and reads `cur->type`, producing the recorded 4-byte heap-use-after-free READ at `xinclude.c:2216`.

bug_description.original: A heap-use-after-free in libxml2's xinclude.c: xmlXIncludeIncludeNode (seen via xmlXIncludeDoProcess/xmlXIncludeLoadFallback) can read memory from XML nodes that have already been freed during XInclude/fallback processing. This use-after-free can cause crashes or memory corruption and may be exploitable.
bug_description.normalized: The staged `poc` is a libxml2 `fuzz/xml` container whose first four bytes decode to the option word `0x2020ffff`; after `XML_PARSE_HUGE` is masked off, the witnessed path still enables `XML_PARSE_XINCLUDE`, `XML_PARSE_NOXINCNODE`, and recovery-style parsing. Its first recorded entity is the main XML document, with an empty URL string followed by an XInclude fragment that begins `<xi:include href="x"` and ends at a nested `<xi:fallback` before the trailing `0xff` bytes. The outer include fails to load resource `x`, so `xmlXIncludeLoadNode()` selects the fallback child and `xmlXIncludeLoadFallback()` allocates one `newctxt`, copies the caller's parse flags into it, and recursively calls `xmlXIncludeDoProcess(newctxt, ctxt->doc, child)` for fallback children while reusing that same context. In one recursive pass, a fallback-child include node is stored in `newctxt->incTab[nr]->ref`; on the witnessed malformed nested-fallback path, `xmlXIncludeLoadFallback()` then sets `newctxt->incTab[nr]->emptyFb = 1`. `xmlXIncludeIncludeNode()` frees that node through the `XML_PARSE_NOXINCNODE` branch but leaves both `newctxt->incTab[nr]->ref` and `emptyFb` intact. Because the same `newctxt` is reused, a later recursive pass again executes the third-phase predicate with `emptyFb != 0`, reloads the freed pointer from `newctxt->incTab[nr]->ref`, and dereferences `cur->type`, matching the saved AddressSanitizer heap-use-after-free.

source.description: First XInclude-side consumption of attacker-controlled document data on the witnessed path. After the parsed main entity yields an `xi:include` node, this statement reads its attacker-supplied `href` and begins constructing the include-processing state that later reaches fallback recursion.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` starts with the little-endian option word `0x2020ffff`, then the `fuzz/xml` main-entity record. The extracted main XML entity begins with `<xi:include href="x" ... <xi:fallback><xi:include href="x"> ...`, so this statement receives the exact attacker-controlled include target `x` from the witness document.

root_cause.description: Root cause fixed by the patch. Vulnerable fallback processing reuses one `newctxt` while recursively processing fallback children one root at a time. Earlier recursive passes can set `emptyFb` and then free a child include node under `XML_PARSE_NOXINCNODE`, but the reused context preserves that slot's `ref` and `emptyFb`, so a later pass re-enters `xmlXIncludeDoProcess` and revisits the dangling entry.
root_cause.note: The staged fix removes the per-child recursion and instead processes the fallback subtree once with `xmlXIncludeDoProcess(newctxt, ctxt->doc, fallback, 1)`. It also adds `if ((skipRoot) && (tree->children == NULL)) return(-1);`, preventing the empty-child-root re-entry that leaves `emptyFb` load-bearing here.

sink.description: Crash sink. `xmlXIncludeIncludeNode` reloads a freed node pointer from the retained include table and immediately reads `cur->type`, producing the saved heap-use-after-free READ.

parser_admitted.description: Project-code parser gate for the staged witness's main XML entity. The malformed container payload still has to reach a top-level `<` so libxml2 enters element parsing and builds the include/fallback node tree used later by XInclude processing.

tainted_value_origin.description: This assignment stores a parsed include node pointer inside an `xmlXIncludeRef` record. When the record is later appended into `ctxt->incTab`, the XInclude context retains that node pointer across recursive processing and later reloads it from the container.

coarse_trace.summary: The libFuzzer-style witness yields a main XML entity containing an `xi:include` with fallback; XInclude processing reads its `href` and records include-node state in the context.

The witness option word is copied into `ctxt->parseFlags` and then into the reused fallback `newctxt`; the outer include load fails, so fallback processing recursively calls `xmlXIncludeDoProcess(newctxt, ctxt->doc, child)` for fallback children while reusing that same context.

One recursive pass stores a fallback-child include node in `newctxt->incTab[nr]->ref`; the malformed nested fallback marks the slot with `emptyFb = 1`, and the `XML_PARSE_NOXINCNODE` branch unlinks and frees that node while leaving `ref` and `emptyFb` behind.

A later recursive pass with the same `newctxt` iterates the full include table again; because `emptyFb` still makes the stale slot eligible, it reloads the dangling `ref` pointer and dereferences `cur->type`, causing the recorded heap-use-after-free.

fine_trace.note: Source. XInclude processing reads the attacker-controlled `href` from the parsed outer `xi:include` element. On the witness path this value is `x`, which drives the later load failure and fallback path.
The outer include node pointer is stored inside a heap `xmlXIncludeRef` and appended to the XInclude context's `incTab`, creating the container state later used by load and include phases.
The outer include load fails for the attacker-supplied target, so control enters fallback handling and selects a fallback child of the outer `xi:include`.

The witness's first four bytes `ff ff 20 20` are read as little-endian option word `0x2020ffff`. After masking out `XML_PARSE_HUGE`, the saved path still carries `XML_PARSE_XINCLUDE` and `XML_PARSE_NOXINCNODE` in `opts`.

depends_on.via: same staged poc bytes that also supplied the include markup

fine_trace.note: The XInclude entry context copies the attacker-derived `flags`/`opts` into `ctxt->parseFlags`, making the input option word available to later XInclude decisions.
Fallback recursion copies the same parse-flag state into the reused `newctxt`, so the recursive include pass sees `XML_PARSE_NOXINCNODE` as well.

Root cause. Vulnerable fallback processing reuses one `newctxt` while recursively processing fallback children one root at a time. The staged patch removes this per-child recursion and processes the fallback subtree once instead.
During one recursive `xmlXIncludeDoProcess(newctxt, ..., child)` pass, a fallback-child include node is stored in the reused `newctxt->incTab` table as `ref`.

fine_trace.code:
ctxt->incTab[nr]->inc = NULL;
ctxt->incTab[nr]->emptyFb = 1;	/* flag empty callback */
fine_trace.note: On the witnessed malformed nested-fallback path, the fallback being loaded for that recursive include has no child nodes. This `else` arm therefore leaves `inc` null and marks the same include-table slot with `emptyFb = 1`, which is the only remaining third-phase eligibility field after `inc` is later cleared again in `xmlXIncludeIncludeNode`.
The first recursive pass enters third-phase inclusion and reaches `xmlXIncludeIncludeNode` for this slot specifically because `emptyFb != 0`.
The include phase reloads that fallback-child node pointer from the context table into local `cur`.

Because the option word propagated through steps 4-6, recursive inclusion takes the `XML_PARSE_NOXINCNODE` branch that removes and frees the include node itself instead of converting it into XInclude marker nodes.
This include pass consumes any `inc` value for the slot and explicitly clears `inc` again, but it does not touch `emptyFb`. The slot therefore keeps `emptyFb == 1` after line 2231.
That branch unlinks and frees the fallback-child include node. The `xmlXIncludeRef` record in `newctxt->incTab[nr]` is not cleared, so `ref` becomes dangling while `emptyFb` remains set.
Because the same `newctxt` survives across fallback-child iterations, a later loop iteration can call `xmlXIncludeDoProcess` again after the free in step 14.

In the later reused-context pass, third-phase inclusion iterates the full `newctxt->incTab` range again. Because `newctxt->incBase` is still `0` and the stale slot still has `emptyFb != 0`, the same entry remains eligible even though line 2231 already cleared `inc`.
The later include pass reloads the same dangling node pointer from the still-eligible slot in `newctxt->incTab[nr]`.
Sink. `cur` is non-null but dangling, so evaluating `cur->type` performs the recorded 4-byte READ from freed node memory.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch is source-consistent with this root cause because it removes the vulnerable per-child fallback recursion and replaces it with one subtree traversal that skips the fallback root, but Stage 02 did not execute the fixed build and therefore does not claim dynamic confirmation.

format.name: libxml2 `fuzz/xml` container
format.contract: The verified trigger is the exact staged witness at `gt_results/secbench_oss_libxml2.ossfuzz-42486565/poc`. Its load-bearing structure is: a four-byte little-endian option word `0x2020ffff` whose surviving bits include `XML_PARSE_XINCLUDE` and `XML_PARSE_NOXINCNODE`; then an empty-string main URL record (`\\\n`); then a main entity string that begins `<xi:include href="x"` and runs into nested fallback/include markup, ending at a nested `<xi:fallback` before the final four `0xff` bytes. This Stage 02 trace is grounded only for that exact malformed nested-fallback witness shape and does not generalize beyond it.
